function.name: cmd_controller_execute
function.description: Executes a system-level command using os.system() on Windows operating systems. It can execute single or multiple commands chained with '&&'. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

command.description: The system command to be executed. To execute multiple commands, separate them with '&&'. For example, 'dir && echo done'.

unit.description: The unit of measurement for the command execution time, such as 'seconds' or 'milliseconds'

message.reasoning:
The user wants to set a timer for 10 seconds using the timeout command. They say "You should use timeout 10." So they want to run a command that will wait 10 seconds. On Windows, the timeout command is used like "timeout /t 10". But they said "timeout 10". That might be Linux? In Linux, "timeout" is a command that runs a command with a time limit. But "timeout 10" alone would just wait 10 seconds? Actually, "timeout 10" will run the command "10"? No. In Linux, "timeout" expects a duration and then a command. If no command is given, it will exit immediately? Let's check: In GNU coreutils, "timeout" requires a command. If you just type "timeout 10", it will error: "timeout: missing command". So maybe they want to run "timeout 10" which will wait 10 seconds? But that doesn't make sense.

Alternatively, maybe they want to run "timeout 10" on Windows, which will wait 10 seconds. On Windows, "timeout" command usage: "timeout /t 10" or "timeout 10" might also work? Actually, Windows timeout command: "timeout /t 10" or "timeout 10" is accepted? I think "timeout 10" is accepted as shorthand for "/t 10". According to docs, "timeout [/t] <seconds> [/nobreak]" So "timeout 10" is equivalent to "timeout /t 10". So yes, that works.

Thus we need to execute the command "timeout 10" on Windows. We can use the provided function cmd_controller_execute. We'll call it with command "timeout 10". The unit can be "seconds" or "milliseconds". We don't need to specify unit. We'll just call it.

We need to produce a JSON response with the function call. The function name is cmd_controller_execute. Provide arguments: command: "timeout 10". The unit optional. We'll not include unit. Then we output the function call.
